chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Nueym al-Sahhaf who said:

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, the merchant of al-Sabiriyyah, died and bequeathed to me, and left a wife for him, and did not leave an heir other than her. So I wrote to al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), and he wrote to me: 'Give the woman one-quarter, and carry the remainder to us.'

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: al-Abd al-Salih (title of Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)
key_terms.بَيَّاعُ السَّابِرِيِّ: merchant of al-Sabiriyyah (a district in Kufa)

ai.seo_question: What is the share of a wife who is the sole heir in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the inheritance distribution for a man leaving only his wife, where she receives one-quarter of the estate while the remainder is transferred to the Imam (peace be upon him). This ruling highlights the Shia concept of the Imam’s right to the surplus estate (al-mughham) when no other heirs exist, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of returning the remainder to the wife or distributing it as residual inheritance. The transmission chain underscores the reliability of the Kufi scholars in preserving these specific fiscal rulings.
